Nestled between the wide expanse of the Grayfynn and the Stoanhall cliffs, a sanctuary of colossal trees form the Arborne woodlands. 
Under these immense canopies, deep sonorous bird song fi lls the air as a troop of aphistus birds rummage through the undergrowth, 
their long talons pulling aside heavy roots to expose the hard shelled nuts and terrestrial fruit that they crave. Th eir innate strength and 
ability to manipulate stubborn roots allows them to make durable nests of living woven roots, packing them with leaf litter to incubate 
their eggs while they venture out in search of food. Th ough generally peaceful creatures, a lifetime of pulling tough roots has bred them 
to be powerfully strong and when roused to defend their kin, their clawed strikes can tear through hide and shell with frightening ease.

Encountering Roaming along the forest ground in troops of 
a dozen kin, the aphistus can often be found by the sound of 
their deep melodious birdsong. While wary of strangers, they 
are generally confi dent in their size and strength to not initially 
flee. If approached slowly, especially when offering food, they 
will quickly calm and may investigate the curious newcomer to 
their woods.
